families.capability: Headers, malformed rows, truncation, encoding, resource limits, and read-only import behavior.
families.sourceContract: Pinned Pi skips malformed JSONL rows, validates the first parsed header before repairing an unterminated tail, and may append a newline during load.
families.difference: Source-pinned oracles confirm header order, CRLF/blank/malformed-line recovery, valid unterminated tails, malformed truncated tails, BOM rejection, read-side newline repair, and acceptance by pinned Pi of a 16 MiB+1 record with a valid descendant. A valid non-entry record before a later session header is rejected by PiSharp. PiSharp preserves source bytes and has 16 MiB record/128 MiB file limits. Exact discovery evidence confirms Pi list streams a 1,048,769-byte header while recent lookup skips it at its 1 MiB scan limit; PiSharp accepts it within its bounds. Direct and file-backed tests cover unsupported version and invalid header types. Corrupt recent candidates are skipped; explicit PiSharp catalog listing reports the path.
families.severity: Safety and compatibility; measure supported outcomes against the exact pin.
families.proposedCorrection: Retain non-mutating import and existing bounds unless a demonstrated supported-data mismatch requires a safe bounded adjustment.
families.regression: PiJsonlSessionInterchangeTests header, identity, BOM, malformed-line, CRLF, tail, entry-size and large-chain cases; SessionCatalogTests large-header and file-backed invalid-header cases; file-store and recovery-process source-preservation tests.

families.capability: Legacy linear entries, generated IDs, parent links, compaction indices, and collision handling.
families.sourceContract: V1 entries receive IDs and sequential parent links; compaction's legacy index maps to the kept entry.
families.difference: Pinned migration assigns generated IDs and sequential parent links, maps valid compaction indices, deletes numeric invalid indices, and retains nonnumeric index fields. PiSharp matches those cases, preserves malformed timestamp/unknown fields, and keeps a read-only load from rewriting the source. Pinned Pi has a collision-check defect that can create duplicate IDs; PiSharp retries IDs to preserve a valid graph.
families.proposedCorrection: Keep the collision retry as an intentional safety-preserving divergence; do not report it as a strict match.
families.status: pinned supported v1 migration verified; invalid compaction-index type semantics verified; ID collision retry and read-only load are classified safety differences

families.capability: V2-to-v3 hookMessage conversion, existing V3 records, unknown fields, round-trip, and repeated migration.
families.sourceContract: V2 hookMessage records become custom; V3 entries remain linked and stable.
families.difference: File-backed pinned migration confirms v1 ID/parent assignment and compaction-index mapping, v2 hookMessage-to-custom conversion, stable v3 entries, repeated reopen behavior, and invalid compaction-index handling. PiSharp matches supported migration semantics. Pi accepts future version 4 and string version "3"; PiSharp rejects them before import.
families.proposedCorrection: Do not change behavior without a reproducible source-pinned mismatch.
families.status: v1-v3 supported migration and idempotent reimport verified; future and noninteger header rejection classified as safety differences

families.capability: Linear and branched records, parent order, selected leaf, append parent, duplicates, orphans, and cycles.
families.sourceContract: The last persisted entry is the active leaf; branch traversal follows parent IDs, including forward references.
families.difference: The pinned graph oracle confirms last-physical-entry selection, forward-parent traversal, missing-parent orphan selection, and subsequent append parent. Exact-pin RPC projection covers nested sibling branches, selected leaf, latest label, active messages and fork messages. Pinned Pi indexes duplicate IDs using the last entry; PiSharp rejects duplicate IDs. Pinned Pi loads cyclic rows but its branch walk has no cycle guard; PiSharp rejects cycles.
families.proposedCorrection: Preserve bounded cycle/duplicate protection and verify ordinary, orphan, and forward-parent observable paths.
families.regression: PiJsonlSessionInterchangeTests selected branch, append parent, forward parent, orphan, duplicate-ID and cycle import cases; ConversationTreeTests cycle and identity guards; RpcSessionEntryProjectorTests and RpcReadCommandsProcessTests for nested branch and latest-label projection.
families.status: ordinary and nested branch reconstruction, selected leaf, append parent, RPC labels, and invalid graph safety verified

families.capability: Active-path messages, context edits, compaction, model/thinking state, tool correlation, and restart continuation.
families.sourceContract: Model context follows the selected parent path, context edits and compaction are applied in order, and incomplete tool calls receive provider-only recovery projection.
families.difference: The b06c1f2 buildSessionContext and streamSimple oracles capture branch context, completed tool history, and orphan-tool recovery across OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions, and Anthropic. The orphan oracle revealed Pi marks Anthropic's synthesized 'No result provided' tool_result as is_error=true; PiSharp originally omitted that flag. ObservedChatClient now marks its provider-only missing result as a ToolFailureException, and the process regression verifies the pinned error flag across the three-API recovery path. A two-run pinned Pi CLI capture now covers get_state, get_messages, get_entries, get_tree and get_fork_messages on a selected branch with sibling branches and labels; matching PiSharp RPC process and projector regressions pass.
families.proposedCorrection: Keep provider-only synthetic missing-result semantics isolated from canonical history; retain the verified physical provider continuations for all three APIs and RPC persisted-state projections.

families.capability: Atomic snapshots, existing-file ownership, stale hash checks, cancellation and failure cleanup.
families.sourceContract: Pi writes JSONL append-only and does not provide PiSharp's snapshot fencing contract.
families.difference: PiSharp atomically publishes private snapshots and rejects stale writers; pinned Pi has no equivalent snapshot fence. A deterministic publication conflict leaves the target intact and removes the temporary file. Cancellation while waiting for the lease preserves the existing snapshot. This is a focused failure-boundary audit of defined publication and cancellation behavior, not a claim that arbitrary device-level failures were injected.
families.proposedCorrection: No change unless a PiSharp failure is demonstrated; keep atomic, private, stale-writer and symlink guards.
families.oracleFixture: Failure injection and reader/writer process probes; source differential classifies the stronger guarantee.
families.status: atomic publication, stale-writer fencing, cancellation, publication failure cleanup and concurrent snapshot reads verified; stronger safety than Pi classified

families.capability: Same-process, cross-process, path alias, cancellation, crash release, and concurrent reads/writes.
families.sourceContract: Pinned Pi does not offer a sibling writer lease or stale-snapshot fence for independently opened managers.
families.difference: PiSharp serializes writers, fences stale snapshots, and passes focused Linux same-process, alias, wait-cancellation, and cross-process tests. The dedicated macOS exact-head workflow runs the corresponding native lock cases.
families.proposedCorrection: Preserve existing coordination; rerun exact-pin same-Pi controls and required Linux process cases; report macOS as unverified.
families.oracleFixture: Existing session-crash-recovery-baseline.md with source pin refreshed.
families.regression: Session lease and store contention process tests.
families.status: linux_process_and_cancellation_cases_verified; macOS coverage configured in exact-head CI

families.capability: Actual process interruption before/during/after tools and recovery without duplicate side effects.
families.sourceContract: An unknown tool outcome must not be treated as success or automatically replayed; completed results stay correlated in restored provider history.
families.difference: PiSharp has actual child-process kills after durable tool intent but before wrapper invocation, during a tool after side effect but before outcome checkpoint, and after the tool outcome checkpoint; restart assertions verify unknown outcomes and no replay. A three-boundary, two-run exact-pin b06c1f2 runtime process oracle confirms ordinary Pi persists the assistant toolCall before invocation, leaves no toolResult after a kill during the side effect, and preserves the correlated toolResult when killed after that checkpoint. Pi does not automatically replay the tool in any of these cases. PiSharp's durable intent/outcome classifications are an intentional stronger-safety behavior, not an attempt to reproduce Pi's less detailed crash record.
families.proposedCorrection: Retain durable tool intent/outcome journal and verify invocation counts at every crash boundary.

families.capability: Create/save/resume/import/export/switch, active-run replacement, state projection and extension restoration.
families.sourceContract: A replacement session is preflighted before active work is cancelled; restored state and project bindings drive the next prompt.
families.difference: Pinned b06c1f2 captures new/resume/fork lifecycle events and state/messages/entries/tree/fork projections twice. PiSharp process coverage verifies new session, valid/invalid switch during blocked work, fork during blocked work, extension restoration, and the next physical provider request after project replacement. The credential-free Pi RPC projection reports the expected unknown model fallback and is limited to persisted-state projection.
families.proposedCorrection: Keep the existing transition owners and provider bindings; the pinned lifecycle/projection and local process evidence cover the required persistence boundary.
